analysis: Changes are limited to the darkbloom CLI sandbox setup flow (TB-013, T-061, A-019). SandboxSetupCommand.swift: for an already-installed add-on, setup now (a) downloads install.sh over HTTPS on every run (withInstaller, line 177) and executes it with `--plan` to compare slot counts, and (b) can then run the full installer with `change.applying(to: options)`. The prompt defaults to yes ([Y/n], SandboxSetupProgress.swift confirm with defaultYes), which is a minor consent weakening. Without a prompt, only slot-adding plans are auto-applied; removals are refused. That decision relies on the installer's self-reported plan and on SandboxSlotChange.onlyAdds, whose source was not supplied. The plan run already happened before consent in the fresh path, so running `--plan` on a set-up Mac adds no new trust beyond T-061's existing download-and-run-as-owner assumption. There is one new behavior: unattended non-TTY runs without --yes can now execute the full install (finding above). I found no changes touching coordinator/provider crypto, attestation, the hold socket (TB-012) or prefix-cache storage (T-041). If jobs are running, the plan check is skipped, and exit 4 now documents that --force is never passed. Still to review: SandboxSlotChange (applying/onlyAdds/command), the installer's integrity verification (signature or hash of install.sh), and TB-013's full text, none of which are in the supplied evidence.

findings.detail: The first-setup path refuses to install without consent: sizeAndConfirm errors with "Confirm in an interactive terminal, or pass --yes" (head lines 275-278). The new already-set-up path in offer() uses `guard !confirmed, interactiveInput else` (line 203). That branch is entered when --yes is passed or when stdin is not a TTY, so a bare `darkbloom sandbox setup` from cron, ssh without a tty, or a script now reaches `install(...)` at line 191 and runs the full downloaded install.sh as the Mac owner without explicit approval. It does so when the installer's own `--plan` output reports a change that only adds slots. The decision comes from output of the remotely fetched script and from `SandboxSlotChange`, which is not in the supplied evidence. This widens the TB-013 / T-061 exposure to a run that previously only reported status. The installer can also update the add-on. Fix: when the input is non-interactive, apply only with explicit --yes and otherwise print the command. Alternatively, run only `--plan` and never `install` unless --yes.
findings.title: Already-set-up `sandbox setup` runs the downloaded installer without --yes whenever stdin is not a terminal
